```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("R/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_small <- simulate_bdat602(n = 10000, seed = 602)
```

## Task 1 — Prepare scaled clustering matrix

```{r task1}
library(dplyr)

hc_df <- health_small |>
  select(age, bmi, income, num_claims, claim_amount) |>
  mutate(
    bmi    = if_else(is.na(bmi),    median(bmi,    na.rm = TRUE), bmi),
    income = if_else(is.na(income), median(income, na.rm = TRUE), income)
  ) |>
  na.omit()

hc_mat <- scale(hc_df)
dim(hc_mat)
```

## Task 2 — Fit k-Means with k = 4

```{r task2}
set.seed(602)
km4 <- kmeans(hc_mat, centers = 4, nstart = 25)

cat("Cluster sizes:", km4$size, "\n")
cat("Total WCSS:   ", round(km4$tot.withinss, 1), "\n")
```

## Task 3 — Cluster profile

```{r task3}
hc_labeled <- health_small |>
  select(age, bmi, income, num_claims, claim_amount, fraud_flag, plan_tier) |>
  mutate(
    bmi    = if_else(is.na(bmi),    median(bmi,    na.rm = TRUE), bmi),
    income = if_else(is.na(income), median(income, na.rm = TRUE), income)
  ) |>
  na.omit() |>
  mutate(cluster = as.factor(km4$cluster))

hc_labeled |>
  group_by(cluster) |>
  summarise(
    n          = n(),
    avg_claim  = round(mean(claim_amount), 0),
    fraud_pct  = round(mean(fraud_flag) * 100, 2),
    avg_age    = round(mean(age), 1)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(avg_claim))
```

The clusters should separate into low-utilisation (young/healthy, low claims), moderate-risk, high-utilisation (older, many claims), and outlier (rare large claims). The cluster with the highest average claims typically also has the highest fraud rate.
